screens.title: Plans and prices
screens.what: The plans side by side, with the one this community falls in by its number of homes, the monthly and annual price of each, and what paying annually saves. Prices are marked provisional until you set them.

screens.title: The free trial, and starting the subscription
screens.what: How many days of the free trial are left and what happens when it ends, then the steps to start: accept the terms, add a bank account or card, confirm. It ends with a receipt and the next renewal date.
screens.reply: Thank you. We have your notes on this screen. We are checking each one against what is built and what is planned, and we will send you a screen-by-screen answer.

screens.title: Billing home: plan, next charge, invoices
screens.what: The board's billing page: the current plan, the next charge and its date, the payment method on file, and every invoice. A board member who is not a billing contact can look but cannot change anything.

screens.title: Billing contacts, and handing over the account
screens.what: Who holds the account: the Account Owner, the backups and any Billing Administrator, with what each may do. Handing the account to someone else waits for that person to accept, and the last backup cannot be removed.

critical.why: Needed by Oct 9: app shell and push notifications.

screens.title: When a payment has not gone through
screens.what: What the board sees when a subscription payment does not go through: the amount owed, the date of the next change and what it will be, with the full schedule below. Paying and reaching support work at every stage, and residents are never affected.

screens.title: Cancelling, and taking the records along
screens.what: What cancelling means, when it takes effect, and what is kept and for how long. The board can take the community's records along first, and can come back later.

screens.title: The HOAhx staff side
screens.what: For HOAhx staff: every community's subscription with its plan, status, next renewal and days past due. Extending a trial, making an exception or restoring access each asks for a written reason, and the reason is kept.

screens.title: Asking for a refund
screens.what: A board member asks to refund a payment: the amount, the reason, and signing in again before it is sent. It shows the most that can be refunded, and refuses a request on the asker's own home or a second request for the same payment.
screens.reply:
Point 3: When a home is sold or the owner moves out with a credit on the account, should the credit go back to the person who paid it? We recommend yes: it is never carried to the next owner, and the treasurer gets a task to refund it to the original payment method, with a second approver.

Point 4: we recommend a change. The ledger records only money that moved: the payment, the credit it left, the refund, the return, each linked to the original. Requests and approvals live in the approval record, which opens from the ledger line and keeps the full history.

Everything else we will build as you wrote it.

screens.title: Approvals waiting for me
screens.what: Every request waiting on this person: who asked, how much, why, and the time left to decide. They sign in again to approve or decline, and cannot act on a request they made or one for their own home.
screens.reply:
Point 5: A refund request nobody approves within 48 hours: should it lapse, as you decided on September 10, or stay waiting and be flagged? We recommend it lapses, with a reminder at 24 hours and a notice to everyone involved when it does.

Everything else we will build as you wrote it.

screens.title: The approval record
screens.what: The permanent record of one refund: who asked and why, who approved, that both signed in again, the amount and where the money went back to. Nothing on it can be edited, and the homeowner gets a receipt.

screens.title: Who may do what
screens.what: Each role down the side and the eight kinds of action across the top. A permission can be taken away from one person, with a reason; nobody can change their own.
screens.reply: Thank you. Most of this is already how the platform works: a refund is requested by one financial user and approved by a different Financial Approver, and nobody can approve their own request or change their own access. We will bring the role grid into line with that rule so the Treasurer's and the approvers' columns match the refund workflow, make sure the last active administrator or Financial Approver can never be removed, explain what the Yes counts mean, and let an authorized user restore a single permission without resetting the whole role. We will report back on each point screen by screen.

screens.title: Exporting a list safely
screens.what: Before a list is downloaded: what the file will contain, what is left out and why, and how many records. The person gives a reason first, and some roles may not export at all.
screens.reply: Thank you. We agree with all four points. The reason will clear whenever the export changes and a fresh reason will be required for each file. Ballot participation (which homes voted, for quorum) will stay separate from vote results, and results will be aggregated with no link from a household to its choice. 'Member since' comes off the default roster export. The permission and the field filtering are enforced on the server, and the download notice will say the file holds community data to share only with authorized people. We will confirm each point when it is built.

screens.title: Naming the two Financial Approvers
screens.what: Why a community needs two Financial Approvers, who is eligible, and who has been chosen. Online payments are held back until two are named.

features.title: Falling behind, payment plans, the ledger and statements

screens.title: Who is behind
screens.what: Every home with an overdue balance: the amount, how long it has been overdue, where the case stands, who is following up and the last thing sent. A notice can go to several homes at once, with a confirmation naming how many.
screens.reply: Thank you. We have your notes on this screen. We are checking each one against what is built and what is planned, and we will send you a screen-by-screen answer.

screens.title: One household's case
screens.what: One home's case from the start: how the balance built up, every notice with its date and whether it arrived, the person who owns the case, and the next step with its date. A payment plan or a waived fee is offered from here.
screens.reply:
Point 5: we recommend a change. Show only 'Delivered' or 'Failed' from the email service, with the exact notice, recipient, method and time. A duplicate second reminder is refused.

Everything else we will build as you wrote it.

screens.title: "I am behind": the homeowner's view
screens.what: What a homeowner who has fallen behind sees: what is owed and what it is made of, the date that matters, what happens then, the choices, and a named person to talk to. Plain wording, no red banners.

screens.title: Setting up a payment plan
screens.what: The treasurer proposes a schedule: how many payments, how much, which dates, and whether late fees pause while the plan is kept. A second person approves it, then the homeowner accepts.
screens.reply: Thank you. We have your notes on this screen. We are checking each one against what is built and what is planned, and we will send you a screen-by-screen answer.

screens.title: A payment plan in progress
screens.what: A plan under way, read as a plan: four of nine paid, the next payment and its date, what remains. The homeowner and the board see the same, including what happens after a missed installment.
screens.reply: Thank you. We have your notes on this screen. We are checking each one against what is built and what is planned, and we will send you a screen-by-screen answer.

screens.title: Waiving a fee or correcting a charge
screens.what: A request to waive a late fee or adjust a balance: the amount, the reason, who is asking and who must approve. It takes two people, the same as a refund, and the homeowner's ledger shows the result.

screens.title: A ledger you can follow
screens.what: Every entry with its date, its kind and the running balance beside it. A correction is a new entry that names the one it corrects; nothing is edited or removed. Drawn once for the homeowner and once for the board.

screens.title: Statements, exports, and matching deposits
screens.what: A statement for each home and a collection summary for the community, each marked with its period. A bank deposit opens to show the payments inside it, with a clear mark where a deposit and the ledger disagree.

screens.title: Upload the spreadsheet and match the columns
screens.what: The board uploads its own CSV or Excel file. HOAhx suggests which column is which; a person confirms or corrects every suggestion. The messy file and the second import are the states to linger on.

screens.title: Check it before it goes in
screens.what: Rows ready, rows needing a decision, rows that cannot go in. A duplicate, a missing detail and a value that only looks wrong are treated as three different things; only a blocked row stops the import.

screens.title: Opening balances: the treasurer signs off
screens.what: The total of all opening balances next to the figure the treasurer expected. Nothing is saved until the treasurer approves it, possibly a different person on a different day.

screens.title: What past imports did, and fixing one
screens.what: Every import on record: who ran it, what it added or changed, and how a mistake is corrected with the correction kept on record.

screens.title: Who has joined
screens.what: Every home and person against the four steps, invited, joined, verified, active; whose invitation has lapsed; sending again to one person or to everyone not yet joined.

screens.title: Someone joined without an invitation
screens.what: What the board sees when a person claims a home without a link, and the plain "we are checking" screen that person sees, ending with the offer of automatic payments.
